abstract: Developing solution-processable molecular materials with long-range magnetic order remains a formidable challenge for molecular electronic and spintronic applications. Herein, we present a diethoxybenzene-fused neutral-radical gold dithiolene complex, Au(4OEt), as a solution-processable single-component molecular antiferromagnet. Owing to its ethoxy substituents, Au(4OEt) adopts a two-dimensional (2D) herringbone arrangement and exhibits semiconducting behavior characteristic of a Mott insulator. Magnetic susceptibility, solid-state 1H NMR, and magnetic torque measurements reveal the emergence of long-range canted antiferromagnetic (CAF) order below approximately 8 K. Combined with transfer-integral calculations and magnetic analyses, these results suggest that constructing a 2D herringbone arrangement of neutral-radical molecules with dominant 2D exchange interactions (|J2| > |J1|) is important for stabilizing the magnetic ordering. Leveraging its solubility, we successfully fabricated solution-processed crystalline thin films that retain the CAF phase. Moreover, the crystalline thin film functions as an ambipolar field-effect transistor (FET). This work thus provides a remarkable example of a solution-processable single-component molecular antiferromagnet exhibiting ambipolar FET characteristics, and establishes a structural design strategy for realizing magnetically ordered crystalline thin films toward future antiferromagnetic devices.
hook: A gold-based radical molecule orders magnetically below 8 K and can be coated from solution.

readout.label: Canted antiferromagnetic order sets in below

summary: Chemists made a neutral-radical gold dithiolene crystal that becomes a canted antiferromagnet at low temperature and also works as an ambipolar transistor in thin films. Magnetic, NMR, and torque measurements support the ordering. The ordering appears only near 8 K, far below any practical device temperature.
title: A Solution-Processable Single-Component Molecular Antiferromagnet.
